## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates your ability to design and implement distributed tracing across a multi-datacenter Docker Swarm environment while meeting strict performance requirements and handling TLS/Nginx integration complexities.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and configuration
- W3C trace context propagation across service boundaries
- OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) exporters and data flow
- Jaeger backend integration for trace storage and visualization
- Docker secrets and configs for secure configuration management
- Multi-datacenter deployment considerations and latency optimization
- Sidecar patterns for collector deployment
- Performance monitoring and overhead control strategies

## Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml skeleton for distributed tracing
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=otel-collector:4317
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-api
      - OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=my-api
    depends_on:
      - otel-collector
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yml:/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml"]

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design end-to-end observability in a multi-DC, TLS-protected microservice environment. It validates understanding of cross-DC trace propagation, per-tenant context isolation, centralized collection, and sampling strategies.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation (automatic and manual)
- OTLP exporter and collector configuration
- Trace context propagation across proxies (W3C traceparent, X-Tenant)
- Tenant-scoped sampling and data governance
- Multi-DC failover and consistent trace routing
- TLS termination at Traefik edge proxy

## Bootstrap Commands

```bash
# Generate TLS certificates
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \\
  -keyout traefik/tls.key -out traefik/tls.crt \\
  -subj "/CN=api.example.com"

# Start the stack
docker-compose up -d
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker
      - --entrypoints.web.address=":443"
      - --entrypoints.web.tls
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./traefik/tls.crt:/tls.crt
      - ./traefik/tls.key:/tls.key
    labels:
      - traefik.tls.creds=true

  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.110.0
    command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml:ro
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP
      - "16686:16686" # Jaeger UI

  api-service:
    build: ./api
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-service
      - OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,b3
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.tls=creds
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.example.com`)

networks:
  default:
    name: dca-network
```

## OTLP Collector Config (tenant-scoped sampling)

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 10s

  probabilistic:
    sampling_percentage: 10

  filter:
    spans:
      exclude:
        match_type: strict
        attributes:
          - key: tenant.id
            value: "low-priority"

exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo:4317
    tls:
      insecure: false

  jaeger:
    endpoint: jaeger:14250
    tls:
      insecure: false

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      - receivers: [otlp]
      - processors: [batch, probabilistic, filter]
      - exporters: [otlp/tempo, jaeger]
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement zero-trust security, multi-tenant isolation, and safe deployment patterns in Docker Swarm with policy-as-code enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Swarm secrets/configs for secure data management
- Sidecar pattern for policy enforcement and logging
- Canary deployments with automatic rollback
- TLS termination at edge proxy
- OPA for real-time authorization decisions

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports: ['443:443']
    secrets:
      - source: tls-cert
        target: /etc/nginx/ssl/tls.crt
      - source: tls-key
        target: /etc/nginx/ssl/tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx-conf
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure
        delay: 5s
        max_attempts: 3
    networks:
      - frontend

  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    environment:
      - TENANT_CONFIGS=/configs/acls.json
    configs:
      - source: tenant-acls
        target: /configs/acls.json
    deploy:
      replicas: 5
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 15s
        failure_action: rollback
        monitor: 30s
        max_failure_ratio: 0.2
      rollback_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
      healthcheck:
        test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
        interval: 10s
        timeout: 5s
        retries: 3
        start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - frontend
      - backend
    volumes:
      - audit-logs:/var/log/audit

  opa:
    image: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
    command: ["run", "--server", "/policies/policy.rego"]
    configs:
      - source: opa-policy
        target: /policies/policy.rego
    environment:
      - OPA_LOG_LEVEL=info
    networks:
      - backend
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8181/v1/data"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  log-collector:
    image: fluent/fluent-bit:latest
    command: ["/fluent-bit/bin/fluent-bit", "--config", "/fluent-bit/etc/fluent-bit.conf"]
    volumes:
      - audit-logs:/var/log/audit
      - ./fluent-bit.conf:/fluent-bit/etc/fluent-bit.conf:ro
    networks:
      - backend
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure

secrets:
  tls-cert:
    external: true
  tls-key:
    external: true

configs:
  nginx-conf:
    external: true
  opa-policy:
    external: true
  tenant-acls:
    external: true

volumes:
  audit-logs:
    driver: local

networks:
  frontend:
    driver: overlay
  backend:
    driver: overlay
    internal: true
```

## fluent-bit.conf
```ini
[SERVICE]
    Flush         5
    Log_Level     info
    Daemon        off

[INPUT]
    Name          tail
    Path          /var/log/audit/*.log
    Tag           audit.*
    Refresh_Interval 10

[OUTPUT]
    Name          file
    Match         audit.*
    Path          /var/log/processed
    File          audit.log
```

## Implementation Details

**OPA Integration**: OPA sidecar loads policies from Docker config and exposes authorization endpoint at `http://localhost:8181/v1/data`. API checks authorization before processing requests.

**Canary Strategy**: 20% rollout (1 out of 5 replicas) every 15 seconds with 30-second health monitoring. Automatic rollback on >20% failures.

**Security**: TLS termination at Nginx edge, secrets management for certificates, internal backend network isolation, per-tenant ACL enforcement.

**Logging**: Audit logs written to shared volume, processed by fluent-bit sidecar for aggregation and forwarding.

## Why This Is Asked

import hashlib

def is_canary(tenant):
  h = int(hashlib.sha256(tenant.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
  return h % 10 == 0  # 10% bucket
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS implementation, Docker secrets management, and edge proxy configuration in a Swarm environment. Evaluates operational skills for secure service-to-service communication.

## Key Concepts
- Docker secrets for TLS certificate management
- Nginx mutual TLS verification and client certificate validation
- Client identity propagation to backend services via HTTP headers

## Code Example
```yaml
# skeleton docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - source: nginx_server_cert
        target: server.crt
      - source: nginx_server_key
        target: server.key
      - source: nginx_ca_cert
        target: ca.pem
    configs:
      - source: nginx_config
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
secrets:
  nginx_server_cert:
    external: true
  nginx_server_key:
    external: true
  nginx_ca_cert:
    external: true
configs:
  nginx_config:
    external: true
```

## Certificate Generation
```bash
# Create private CA
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca.key -out ca.pem

# Generate server certificate
openssl genrsa -out server.key 2048
openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out server.crt -days 365

# Generate client certificate
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.crt -days 365

# Create Docker secrets
docker secret create nginx_server_cert server.crt
docker secret create nginx_server_key server.key
docker secret create nginx_ca_cert ca.pem
```

## Testing Commands
```bash
# Test with client certificate
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Test without client certificate (should fail)
curl --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Verify client identity header
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api -v | grep X-Client-Subject
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce per-tenant access controls with runtime configuration sourced from Docker Configs. It covers TLS termination via Traefik, Traefik routing configuration, and implementing a low-friction policy engine directly in the API.

## Key Concepts
- Docker Configs for centralized policy data
- Per-tenant authorization and path-based access control
- Traefik TLS fronting and reverse proxying
- API-side policy enforcement
- Live configuration rotation via Docker Configs

## Bootstrap Commands
```bash
# Create Docker Config for tenant policies
echo '{"tenants": {"acme": {"allowedPaths": ["/api/orders", "/api/invoices"]}, "globex": {"allowedPaths": ["/api/reports"]}}}' | docker config create policies.json -

# Create network for the cluster
docker network create docker-dca
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton
```yaml
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker
      - --entrypoints.websecure.address=:443
      - --entrypoints.web.address=:80
      - --tls.certificates.tls.certFile=/certs/server.crt
      - --tls.certificates.tls.keyFile=/certs/server.key
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./certs:/certs:ro
    configs:
      - source: policies
        target: /etc/traefik/policies.json
    networks:
      - docker-dca

  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    environment:
      - POLICY_FILE=/run/secrets/policies.json
    configs:
      - source: policies
        target: /run/secrets/policies.json
    labels:
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.rule=PathPrefix(`/api`)"
      - "traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=3000"
    networks:
      - docker-dca

configs:
  policies:
    external: true

networks:
  docker-dca:
    driver: bridge
```

## Policy Engine Implementation
```javascript
const fs = require('fs');

const policies = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.POLICY_FILE, 'utf8'));

app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const tenant = req.headers['x-tenant'];
  const path = req.path;
  
  if (!tenant) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Missing X-Tenant header' });
  }
  
  const tenantPolicy = policies.tenants?.[tenant];
  if (!tenantPolicy) {
    return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Unknown tenant' });
  }
  
  const allowedPaths = tenantPolicy.allowedPaths || [];
  const isAllowed = allowedPaths.some(allowed => path.startsWith(allowed));
  
  if (!isAllowed) {
    return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Access denied' });
  }
  
  next();
});
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question explores per-tenant data residency routing via a lightweight sidecar proxy, complementing existing TLS and tenant controls. It tests understanding of runtime configuration, routing decisions, and reliability in multi-DC environments.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-based routing across data centers using a sidecar proxy
- Docker Config-driven policy enforcement with fallback logic
- Traffic rewriting and backend selection with minimal downtime
- Observability hooks and test planning for per-tenant routing

## Code Example
```yaml
# Envoy bootstrap configuration
static_resources:
  listeners:
    - name: listener_0
      address:
        socket_address:
          address: 0.0.0.0
          port_value: 8000
      filter_chains:
        - filters:
            - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
              typed_config:
                "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
                stat_prefix: ingress_http
                route_config:
                  name: tenant_routing
                  virtual_hosts:
                    - name: service
                      domains:
                        - "*"
                      routes:
                        - match:
                            prefix: "/"
                          route:
                            cluster: primary_cluster
                http_filters:
                  - name: envoy.filters.http.lua
                    typed_config:
                      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
                      inline_code: |
                        function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
                          local tenant_id = request_handle:headers():get("X-Tenant-ID")
                          local handle = assert(io.popen("docker config ls --format '{{.Name}} {{.ID}}' | grep tenant_region"))
                          local result = handle:read("*a")
                          handle:close()
                          
                          -- Parse Docker config for tenant mapping
                          if tenant_id and result:match(tenant_id) then
                            local region = result:match(tenant_id .. ":%s*(%S+)")
                            if region == "secondary" then
                              request_handle:headers():add("X-Upstream-Cluster", "secondary_cluster")
                            end
                          end
                        end

  clusters:
    - name: primary_cluster
      type: EDS
      lb_policy: ROUND_ROBIN
      endpoints:
        - locality:
            region: primary
          lb_endpoints:
            - endpoint:
                address:
                  socket_address:
                    address: api-primary
                    port_value: 8080

    - name: secondary_cluster
      type: EDS
      lb_policy: ROUND_ROBIN
      endpoints:
        - locality:
            region: secondary
          lb_endpoints:
            - endpoint:
                address:
                  socket_address:
                    address: api-secondary
                    port_value: 8080
```

```
